title: KAFKA-21204: Return the fetchable max timestamp from ListOffsets
body:
## Summary
- ListOffsets searched past the high watermark for `MAX_TIMESTAMP` and then returned `-1`, hiding an earlier timestamp the client is allowed to read.
- Pass `lastFetchableOffset` into the log search. When that bound is behind the log end, return the largest timestamp still inside it, including a max that lives in an earlier segment.

## Test plan
- [x] `UnifiedLogTest.testFetchOffsetByTimestampRespectsFetchableBound`
- [x] `UnifiedLogTest.testMaxTimestampBelowBoundCanComeFromEarlierSegment`
- [x] `UnifiedLogTest.testFetchOffsetByTimestampWithMaxTimestampIncludesTimestamp`
- [x] `FileRecordsTest.testSearchForTimestamp`
- [x] `:storage:checkstyleMain`, `:storage:checkstyleTest`, `:clients:checkstyleMain`, spotless on the touched modules
Reviewers : @junrao

Reviewers: Jun Rao <junrao@gmail.com>

files.patch:
@@ -1463,7 +1463,7 @@ class Partition(val topicPartition: TopicPartition,
 
     def getOffsetByTimestamp: OffsetResultHolder = {
       logManager.getLog(topicPartition)
-        .map(log => log.fetchOffsetByTimestamp(timestamp, remoteLogManager.asInstanceOf[Option[AsyncOffsetReader]].toJava))
+        .map(log => log.fetchOffsetByTimestamp(timestamp, remoteLogManager.asInstanceOf[Option[AsyncOffsetReader]].toJava, lastFetchableOffset))
         .orElse(new OffsetResultHolder(Optional.empty[FileRecords.TimestampAndOffset]()))
     }
